taxonomy.subtopic: Accessory atrioventricular pathway and ventricular preexcitation

questions.stem_html:
A 20-year-old man has sudden episodes of rapid regular palpitations. Between episodes, ECG shows a short PR interval, a slurred initial upstroke of the QRS complex, and a mildly widened QRS. An electrophysiology diagram shows a muscular connection between atrium and ventricle outside the atrioventricular node.

Which property of this connection creates the baseline ECG pattern?

options.text_html: It accelerates phase 4 depolarization in the sinoatrial node
It blocks retrograde conduction through the His-Purkinje system
It conducts atrial impulses to ventricular myocardium without the normal atrioventricular nodal delay
It prolongs ventricular action-potential duration by blocking potassium channels
It causes intermittent failure of atrial impulses to reach the ventricles

questions.explanation_html: The accessory pathway bypasses the AV node and activates part of the ventricle early through slow cell-to-cell myocardial conduction. This produces a short PR interval and delta wave. Ventricular preexcitation occurs because the bypass tract lacks the physiologic AV nodal delay.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Faster sinus automaticity would increase rate but would not produce a delta wave or short PR interval.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Retrograde blockade does not explain antegrade ventricular preexcitation.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Potassium-channel blockade prolongs QT rather than creating a delta wave.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Conduction failure produces AV block, which lengthens or interrupts conduction rather than shortening PR.

questions.educational_objective: Explain the short PR interval and delta wave in WPW as early ventricular activation through an accessory atrioventricular pathway.
